findings.title: Non-superseded is treated as active without validating successor disposition
findings.observed: validate checks history[sid].disposition != superseded, not disposition == active. In-memory changes to a frozen successor disposition quarantined/inactive/unknown all pass, and the returned historical link still advertises that successor as activeCanonicalSuccessors. load_reviewed pins mapping/review/report/source files but not current successor disposition content; it delegates this same check. The historical original disposition is exact equality checked; successor disposition is not. Current baseline successor states remain active; this finding is the required tamper guard gap, not a baseline semantic failure.
findings.relatedObservations: Changes to successor evidenceResultPreserved/originalRequirementsPreserved/activeSettingLinks/countsTowardAcceptance also pass because that metadata is not checked. Native successor body/result/requirements/scope are independently hash-pinned, and every returned historical link retains countsTowardAcceptance:false. Thus no false acceptance or native result is claimed from those metadata controls.
findings.consequence: A later successor quarantine or malformed/unknown disposition can be advertised as reviewed active lineage, violating fail-closed active-successor preparation. This guard is not yet root-integrated, so no existing root promotion occurred.
findings.requiredCorrection: Require exactly the supported active disposition for every successor, fail closed on unknown or all nonactive states. Validate current disposition metadata consistency with the pinned native body/requirements and expected setting links (or pin an independently reviewed complete successor-disposition slice), while retaining historical nonacceptance. At minimum the active-state contradiction must reject; explicitly document any intentionally ignored successor metadata rather than claiming it preserved.
